name: French
strapline: Bonjour, le monde. Make connections through language.
intro: French belongs to diverse communities in Europe, Africa, the Caribbean and beyond. Learn to communicate an idea clearly and listen with curiosity. Suggested BGE units can be adapted around the class’s interests. The national Modern Languages framework applies to French; the department confirms texts, sequence and available pathways.

bge.title: Moi et les autres
bge.question: How can we find something in common?
bge.task: Make a fictional identity card, then interview a partner about two interests using “Qu’est-ce que tu aimes… ?”.
bge.extend: Ask a follow-up question using something your partner said.

bge.title: Mon quartier idéal
bge.question: What would make a place better?
bge.task: Draw an imaginary neighbourhood. Describe what there is, where it is and one reason to visit.
bge.extend: Compare it with another imaginary town using “plus… que”.

bge.title: À table
bge.question: How can language help us make a choice?
bge.task: Create a café menu with prices. Role-play an order, clarify an ingredient and check the total.
bge.extend: Write a short review with a specific reason for your recommendation.

bge.title: La francophonie
bge.question: Who uses French, and how?
bge.task: Choose two French-speaking places. Use a cultural organisation’s resource to compare one aspect of daily life.
bge.extend: Explain why one person or celebration cannot represent everyone in a country.

senior.title: French — Modern Languages
senior.explain: These national courses develop receptive and productive language skills. National 4 adds an assignment; your teacher selects appropriate topics.
senior.assessment: Internal unit assessment; National 4 also requires the added value assignment.

senior.title: French — Modern Languages
senior.explain: The four contexts frame language learning. Suggested cultural investigations here are optional enrichment, not an additional national unit.
senior.assessment: Reading and writing paper, listening paper, writing assignment and talking performance. Follow current controlled-assessment rules.

senior.title: French — Modern Languages
senior.explain: Develop richer language, inference and discussion across the national contexts. Your class’s chosen examples are confirmed by the department.
senior.assessment: Reading and directed writing, listening, writing assignment and talking performance. Check current official guidance.

skills.title: Listen in layers
skills.explain: First listen for the topic, then for specific detail.
skills.try: Predict three words, listen once without a transcript and write a short gist.
skills.check: Replay to confirm details and notice negatives or time expressions.

skills.title: Build a reusable phrase bank
skills.explain: Learn a useful chunk with its meaning and an example.
skills.try: Save an opinion, a reason and a contrasting connector.
skills.check: Can you adapt the phrase to a new topic without copying a whole answer?

skills.title: Read for evidence
skills.explain: Look for who, when and why before translating every word.
skills.try: Underline the phrase supporting each reading answer.
skills.check: Check pronouns, negatives and whether the event is past, present or future.

skills.title: Speak to communicate
skills.explain: A clear message matters more than racing through a script.
skills.try: Record 30 seconds, listen and improve one pronunciation or verb.
skills.check: Can a listener understand your idea, reason and follow-up question?

practice.question: Read: “J’habite près du collège, donc j’y vais à pied. Quand il pleut, je prends le bus.” How does the speaker usually travel, and when does this change?
practice.hint: “À pied” and “quand il pleut” are the key phrases.
practice.answer: They usually walk because they live near school; they take the bus when it rains. Include the condition rather than saying they always take the bus.
practice.extend: Write a sentence comparing this journey with your own or a fictional journey.

practice.question: Improve: “J’aime la musique. C’est bien.” Give a specific reason.
practice.hint: Use “parce que” and explain an effect or benefit.
practice.answer: For example, “J’aime la musique parce que cela m’aide à me détendre.” This gives a clear reason. Other accurate reasons are equally valid.
practice.extend: Add a different opinion using “cependant” and check your verb agreement.

practice.question: What is the difference between “Je joue au foot” and “J’ai joué au foot”?
practice.hint: Look for the auxiliary and past participle.
practice.answer: The first describes playing football in the present or habitually. The second says “I played/have played football”. “Ai” plus “joué” signals the perfect tense.
practice.extend: Write a present, past and future sentence about an activity, with a time phrase in each.

resources.title: TV5MONDE video learning
resources.task: Choose A1 or A2, watch once for gist, then complete the listening activities. Arabic navigation is available on the provider’s site.

resources.title: RFI: Le français facile
resources.task: Choose a short audio with a transcript. Listen first, then highlight five useful phrases in the text.

resources.title: Institut français UK
resources.task: Find a cultural event and produce a short French invitation with time, place and reason to attend.

resources.title: TV5MONDE dictionary
resources.task: Check a word in context and use it in an original sentence.

resources.title: National 5 Modern Languages
resources.task: Try French reading or listening practice and explain why each detail earns credit.

ipad.title: My listening laboratory
steps: Listen before viewing the transcript and record your understanding.
Compare with the transcript and colour-code new expressions.
ipad.evidence: A gist, three checked details and two phrases to reuse.

ipad.title: A conversation that grows
steps: Create a short prompt card without full sentences.
Record a fictional conversation with permission.
Repeat after improving one tense and one follow-up question.
ipad.evidence: Two recordings and a brief reflection on what improved.

ipad.title: A visual phrase journey
steps: Photograph objects or signs where photography is permitted.
Add accurate target-language captions using a checked dictionary.
Record yourself explaining a connection between the images.
ipad.evidence: A small narrated slide deck; no identifiable people or personal addresses.

careers.title: Tourism and hospitality
careers.linkToLearning: Listening, welcoming visitors and clarifying requests improve service.
careers.nextStep: Explore college travel or hospitality courses and tourism apprenticeships.

careers.title: International business
careers.linkToLearning: Language and cultural awareness support customers and partnerships.
careers.nextStep: Compare business-with-languages degrees and work-based business routes.

careers.title: Translation and communication
careers.linkToLearning: Accurate meaning, research and register matter more than word substitution.
careers.nextStep: Investigate language degrees and practise editing a short bilingual explanation.

careers.title: Community and public service
careers.linkToLearning: Respectful communication helps schools, health and community organisations.
careers.nextStep: Explore college routes and ask how language skills complement another profession.

parentTip: Ask your young person to teach you three useful phrases. Let them replay a short recording and identify one improvement. Encourage a small daily practice habit and curiosity about different communities.
